findings.issue_text: [High/bug] CalendarService.ts:253 & :314 — In updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch using externalCalendarId only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match anything, resulting in undefined calendarId and breaking deletes/updates for events without a stored external id

[Critical/bug] create.handler.ts:150-152 — Logic inversion: slug and requestedSlug are now included when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED instead of when billing is disabled, flipping which environments get a slug and appearing unrelated to the PR's purpose

[High/bug] EventManager.ts (update, ~line 510-545) — credential declared outside the loop is reused across iterations; if a reference's credential lookup fails, a stale credential from a previous iteration is passed to updateEvent, updating the wrong calendar

[Medium/bug] EventManager.ts (update, ~line 540) — updateEvent is called with an undefined credential even when credentialFromDB is null/invalid, causing a runtime crash masked by the catch block as a 'failed' result

[Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts:97-127 — With multiple destination calendars, the organizer email is always taken from the first destination calendar even when the event is created on a different host's calendar, causing mismatched organizer email for secondary hosts

[Medium/data] handleNewBooking.ts:1871-1877 — Only the first destination calendar id is persisted to the booking, so cancel/edit flows reconstructing from booking.destinationCalendar only know about the first host's calendar

[Medium/bug] handleCancelBooking.ts (~line 430) — DB-fetched credential is passed to getCalendar without including the app relation, so it may lack the appName info needed to instantiate the correct calendar service, causing cancel failures

[Medium/bug] EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents, DB fallback) — manually reconstructed credential object omits fields and may have a mismatched key type (Prisma Json), so calendar services may fail at runtime; should use the existing typed helper instead of ad-hoc object construction in three places

[Low/bug] requestReschedule.handler.ts:240 — destinationCalendar fallback dropped the user fallback entirely; if bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar is null the event now gets [] while other handlers still fall back to user.destinationCalendar, making it inconsistent

[Medium/test_gap] No tests added for the core behavior change of multiple destination calendars on collective bookings; only test change is a snapshot update that locks in the new shape without verifying multi-host creation or the externalCalendarId fallback paths

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] CalendarService.ts:253 & :314 — In updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback branch using externalCalendarId only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it can never match anything, resulting in undefined calendarId and breaking deletes/updates for events without a stored external id

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. But that fallback branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === undefined/null` and will almost always return `undefined`. This prevents using the event’s destination calendar when no `externalCalendarId` is provided (e.g., older references), causing updates/deletes to target the default (`primary`) or an undefined calendarId rather than the actual calendar where the event was created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] EventManager.ts (update, ~line 510-545) — credential declared outside the loop is reused across iterations; if a reference's credential lookup fails, a stale credential from a previous iteration is passed to updateEvent, updating the wrong calendar

adjudication.rationale: In the updated loop, `credential` is reassigned on every iteration via `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0];`, which overwrites any prior value (it becomes `undefined` if not found). So a previous iteration’s credential is not “reused” as a stale value. While there *is* a potential issue that `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is called even if `credential` remains `undefined` after both in-memory and DB lookup fail, that is a different bug than the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] EventManager.ts (update, ~line 540) — updateEvent is called with an undefined credential even when credentialFromDB is null/invalid, causing a runtime crash masked by the catch block as a 'failed' result

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same bug: when a credentialId is present but the credential lookup fails (null/invalid), updateEvent is still invoked with an undefined credential, potentially causing a runtime error/crash (even if caught/masked).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] CalendarService.ts:97-127 — With multiple destination calendars, the organizer email is always taken from the first destination calendar even when the event is created on a different host's calendar, causing mismatched organizer email for secondary hosts

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` selects the target `calendarId` based on `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, but the organizer attendee email is derived from `mainHostDestinationCalendar` which is always the first element of `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ...`). This means when creating an event for a non-first destination calendar (secondary host), the organizer email can incorrectly use the first destination calendar’s `externalId` instead of the one matching `credentialId`, causing the mismatch described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] handleNewBooking.ts:1871-1877 — Only the first destination calendar id is persisted to the booking, so cancel/edit flows reconstructing from booking.destinationCalendar only know about the first host's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the PR builds `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (including pushing additional team member destination calendars for COLLECTIVE), but when persisting to the Booking it only connects the first one: `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`. This means any additional destination calendars used to create events are not persisted on the booking’s `destinationCalendar` relation, so later code that derives `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (now wrapped into a single-element array in multiple handlers) can only ever recover the first one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] handleCancelBooking.ts (~line 430) — DB-fetched credential is passed to getCalendar without including the app relation, so it may lack the appName info needed to instantiate the correct calendar service, causing cancel failures

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the new fallback path fetches a credential via `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then passes that raw record to `getCalendar(calendarCredential)`. Unlike the similar new logic added in `EventManager` (which `include`s `app.slug` and constructs a `CredentialWithAppName`), this DB-fetched credential lacks any `app`/`appName` context. Given the refactor in this diff toward using `CredentialWithAppName` to select the correct calendar integration, this inconsistency can cause `getCalendar` to instantiate the wrong service (or fail) for credentials where `type` alone is insufficient (notably “other_calendar” style integrations), leading to cancel/delete failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents, DB fallback) — manually reconstructed credential object omits fields and may have a mismatched key type (Prisma Json), so calendar services may fail at runtime; should use the existing typed helper instead of ad-hoc object construction in three places

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce ad-hoc reconstruction of a `credential` object from `prisma.credential.findUnique(...)` in at least two places in `packages/core/EventManager.ts` (inside `createAllCalendarEvents` and the calendar-reference update loop). That’s a concrete maintainability/consistency issue (duplicated manual mapping) and could lead to subtle type/shape drift vs whatever `getCalendar`/`CredentialWithAppName` expects. However, the finding’s stronger claim that it *verifiably* “omits fields” or has a “mismatched key type” causing runtime failures cannot be confirmed from this diff alone because the required credential shape and runtime usage aren’t shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] requestReschedule.handler.ts:240 — destinationCalendar fallback dropped the user fallback entirely; if bookingToReschedule.destinationCalendar is null the event now gets [] while other handlers still fall back to user.destinationCalendar, making it inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: In requestReschedule.handler.ts the event is now built with `destinationCalendar: bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []`, so when the booking has no destinationCalendar it becomes an empty array. Multiple other handlers in this diff explicitly fall back to `user.destinationCalendar` (e.g. confirm/editLocation/payments/deleteCredential), but requestReschedule does not, which can result in reschedule-request flows losing the organizer’s default destination calendar selection and behaving inconsistently. (The finding’s wording about “dropped” is a bit off—pre-change code shown in the diff didn’t include a user fallback either—but the inconsistency/empty-array behavior is verifiable.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests added for the core behavior change of multiple destination calendars on collective bookings; only test change is a snapshot update that locks in the new shape without verifying multi-host creation or the externalCalendarId fallback paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces substantial new core logic for handling multiple destination calendars (e.g., `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` becomes an array, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and may fetch missing credentials from DB, and `CalendarManager.createEvent`/Google `createEvent` now pass/select calendar by `credential.id` and `destination.externalId`). However, the only visible test adjustment is a Playwright snapshot shape change (`destinationCalendar: null` -> `destinationCalendar: []` in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts`) which does not assert multi-destination creation for COLLECTIVE bookings or the new `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId` propagation and fallback paths. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not an immediately verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.
